action_summary: Revision 10 of the census, plus the referee repair that makes it readable. The new section lists all 28 tasks with the capability that ACTUALLY answered each and the defect that answer exposes: 10 pass, 18 fail, and the 18 are 5 defects, not 18 missing capabilities. P1 a shell command is invented from a verb, with no check that the verb's OBJECT is something a command can act on -- 5 rows including the only false pass, and the reason the already-written SQL adapter is withheld ('Remove the SQL injection' becomes `rm <db.py>`). P2 the request's mode (ask vs change) is not a routing key -- 5 rows answered by an analyser. P3 the owner exists and declares an artifact no sentence can state -- 4 rows. P4 a stub reports verified and edits nothing -- 1 row. P5 no owner -- 3 rows. Also measured: routing costs 99% of every wall clock (a 0.2-2 ms adapter answers in 150-450 ms); one task produced no verdict at all in 180 s; and three fixtures (fx_move, fx_deadcode, fx_signature) shipped tests that import a class the code never defines, so their baseline suite was red before any edit and a perfect repair scored the same as a broken one. Those three are repaired here and the census is unchanged at 10/28 -- the rows still fail, now for the real reason. No capability is added and no score is claimed.
